text:
Sunset is at 4:34, and with the cloud deck this thick, don't expect much color. It's 45 right now and will slide toward the upper 30s tonight, with a low around 37.

The rain fills in after 7 and looks steadiest from about 9 to midnight, then tapers off through the small hours. Most of it should come to around a tenth of an inch, maybe a touch more. The European model is a lot wetter than the American one, so I'd lean toward steady rain rather than just sprinkles. Grab the umbrella if you're heading out tonight.

Sunday starts damp, with a stray shower possible until about 9, then it turns drier. Skies stay mostly cloudy, but the afternoon is your best window for a walk or errands, with a high near 53. That's a rinse-and-repeat pattern, though. Showers return after 7 Sunday night, and Monday brings more light rain. Plan outdoor time for Sunday afternoon and keep the jacket handy.

week.blurb: Cloudy with a high near 51 and just a stray shower this afternoon, then rain likely tonight, a tenth to a quarter inch.

Mostly cloudy with a high near 52, and a shower possible from early afternoon into the evening.
Veterans Day looks partly sunny and cooler, high near 48, with a spotty shower possible and a chilly night near 30.
Looks like a cloudy, colder Thursday, high near 45, with a rain-snow mix possible after dark and a low near 26.
Trending cloudy and raw, high near 43, with a chance of rain or wet snow mixing in, mostly toward evening.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: We'll be in a bit of a rinse-repeat pattern through at least Tuesday. Two upper lows will merge early this week, and patches of embedded moisture will result in showery conditions. There will be lulls in activity, though, with the greatest chances of limited shower activity Sunday afternoon and Tuesday morning. During the day on Tuesday, a shortwave ridge will build ahead of an incoming low that will open into a trough as it shifts east- southeast. This will result in flattened 500mb heights with a trend towards decreasing heading into the middle of next week. Forecast high temperatures will be in the mid-40s to mid-50s, and overnight lows will range near 30 to near 40 for the next 3-4 days. KEY MESSAGE 2: Cyclonic flow centered over eastern Canada will swing a couple shortwaves through northern New York and Vermont next mid week. The first is modeled to swing through on Tuesday night, resulting in chance of precipitation 30-60%, locally 55-85% across the northern Greens. As temperatures fall into the upper 20s to mid 30s, some of the higher elevations could see some snow mixing in with the rain early Wednesday morning. Depending on the strength of high pressure to our south, there's the chance for additional showers during the daytime Wednesday hours as well (15-45% chance), though most spots should see temperatures warm into the 40s and lower 50s that afternoon, resulting in mainly rain. Model consensus really falls apart by Wednesday night, but the main agreements relate to brief weak ridging over the area into Thursday, then a deep trough or closed low developing over the midwest towards Friday. Based on this, chances for precip run 10-40% for the late week accompanied by highs upper 30s to near 50 F and lows in the teens to near 30 F. Models are suggesting a coastal storm could set up next weekend to bring more steady precipitation to the region, but the details are not clear that far out.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - The recent stretch of 60s and even 70s was very pleasant for being outdoors, and it felt like it was September again. However, it’s November, and it’s going to feel a lot more like it in the days to come. Today will start off early with mostly cloudy skies and a few showers, then showers will become more numerous through the day. It will be cooler with highs in the 50s. Showers will continue overnight, then move out from west to east Sunday morning. Up to a half inch of rain is possible, though it looks a touch drier than previously expected. A brief period of snow is still possible in the Northeast Kingdom and Coos County, New Hampshire Sunday morning, though any accumulation now looks confined to the White Mountains with a trace to 3 inches, the highest amounts at the summits. Sunday afternoon will be partly sunny with highs in the 40s. Another system will bring additional rain on Monday, though it will be on the lighter side. Highs will be in the 40s and lows will be in the 30s. A few breaks of sun are possible on Tuesday, but scattered showers are likely, especially north. More widely scattered showers are expected on Veterans Day, though the mountains could get snow showers with colder highs in the upper 30s to low 40s. Dry weather is expected for Thursday and Friday, but temperatures will continue their downward trend. Thursday will be mostly cloudy, and Friday will be partly sunny. Highs will only be in the 30s to low 40s both days, so make sure to have a solid jacket if you head outdoors. Lows will be in the 20s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-07T13:45:00Z — same caveat): Cloudy and cooler Saturday, showers gradually fill in — This weekend turns much cooler and unsettled, an an upper-level low brings the return of more seasonable air for early November. Saturday will feature a mainly cloudy sky, highs in the low 50s and a stiff north breeze. Scattered showers arrive first in New York, gradually spreading east during the afternoon and evening. Tonight stays cloudy, with passing rain showers and lows in the 30s to near 40. Mountain snowflakes, and a light accumulation, are possible for northern summits (especially in New Hampshire). Sunday looks drier, with morning clouds giving way to a window of afternoon sun — which may illuminate a light dusting of summit snow. Highs will be near 50. Early next week looks seasonably cool, with several chances for rain showers and minor mountain snow accumulations between Monday and Veterans Day. Highs reach the 40s to around 50. Drier weather looks to return by Thursday and Friday. However, expect lots of clouds and chillier temperatures. Highs will be near 40.
